# Runbook — Job-schedule importer (`schedule_poll`) (an uploaded schedule PDF stuck / refused / dark) (Successor-Remediation, Op Stds §43)

>   - Field-ops sync — portal job/hours/materials/equipment/incidents to Smartsheet → schedule-poll screens, OCRs, and files an uploaded project-schedule PDF → “An uploaded schedule was refused (unreadable or MALICIOUS), failed integrity, or imported with an active-content warning.”
>   - Field-ops sync — portal job/hours/materials/equipment/incidents to Smartsheet → schedule-poll screens, OCRs, and files an uploaded project-schedule PDF → “The daemon's grid post for a schedule was permanently refused by the Worker (an HTTP 4xx), and the schedule stopped retrying.”

A §43 successor-remediation entry, written for the **Successor-Operator**: a trained
operator who runs Claude Code and reads Smartsheet rows + alert emails, but does **not**
read code. Claude loads the relevant block to drive a Tier-2 repair; the operator sees the
ITS_Errors / ITS_Review_Queue / ITS_Daemon_Health evidence and approves. The §42
code-reader rationale lives in the module docstring of `field_ops/schedule_poll.py`, and
the design record is [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-job-schedule-payment-tracking.md).

`field_ops/schedule_poll.py` is part of the **generation half of the External Send Gate**
(FM v11 Invariant 1) — it is AI-free and customer-send-free. The office uploads a
project-schedule PDF through the portal; the Cloudflare Worker
(`safety_portal/worker/fieldops_schedules.ts`) queues it **send-free** in D1 and signs it
(`schedule:v1`); this launchd daemon (`org.solutionsmith.its.schedule-poll`, every 120 s)
is the Mac-side consumer, behind ONE gate (`field_ops.schedule_poll.polling_enabled`).
Per document it:

1. **Claims** the row, pulls the bytes, and **verifies** them (schedule:v1 HMAC **and** a
   separate length + SHA-256 recompute) — a failure here is an INTEGRITY event
   (Symptom 4), never processed further.
2. **Screens** the document (§34 — the same screener as PO attachments, vendor estimates
   and manifests; the optional ClamAV layer reuses
   `po_materials.po_attach_screen.clamav_enabled`).
3. **Reads the pages inside a killable child process.** Most schedule exports carry no
   real text — the table is drawn as shapes — so the daemon photographs each page and
   reads it with the Mac's own on-device text recognition (no cloud AI anywhere in this
   lane). That work runs somewhere the daemon can kill; if the child dies or times out,
   the document is refused — the daemon is never harmed (Symptom 5).
4. **Parses** the reconstructed table, files the ORIGINAL PDF to Box under
   `<job>/Schedules/`, posts the grid + page pictures back, and marks the schedule
   `parsed`.

**What it deliberately does NOT do:** it never commits a task and never trusts its own
reading. The text recognition can misread a digit while looking confident, so every cell
waits for a person on the validate screen, checked against the page picture beside it.
Nothing this daemon does changes a job's task list — that happens later, when a person
commits.

## What is Tier-2 and what escalates

**Tier-2 (you can do this):** re-run a cycle, read a Review-Queue row, clear a one-shot
flag to retry a *readability* refusal, ask the office for a fresh export, confirm the
gate and the launchd job.

**Escalates to Seth (Tier-3), always:**
- Any **integrity failure** (Symptom 4) — a signature or digest mismatch means the row or
  the bytes disagree with what was signed. Do not clear its flag.
- Any **MALICIOUS** screen verdict (Symptom 3) — it names the uploading account; that
  account is reviewed before uploads resume.
- `schedule_bearer_rejected` — a credential problem (a FIXED high-capability class).
- **Turning the gate ON for the first time** — a capability activation.

---

## Symptom 1 — "Nothing happens when the office uploads a schedule"

**Evidence:** no `schedule_poll` row in ITS_Daemon_Health, or its heartbeat is older than
~10 minutes; the schedule stays `pending` in the portal.

Two switches must BOTH be on, and a daemon with the gate off is deliberately silent — it
writes no heartbeat and no watchdog marker, because a dark lane is an intentional state,
not a fault. Check, in order:

1. **The gate.** ITS_Config → `field_ops.schedule_poll.polling_enabled`, Workstream
   `field_ops`. Read the row's **Description** as well as its value.
2. **The launchd job.** `launchctl list | grep schedule-poll`. If absent:
   `scripts/launchd/install.sh load org.solutionsmith.its.schedule-poll`.

If both are on and there is still no heartbeat, look for `schedule_creds_missing`
(CRITICAL) in ITS_Errors — see Symptom 6.

## Symptom 2 — "An upload is stuck on 'claimed'"

**Evidence:** the schedule shows `claimed` in the portal for more than a few cycles;
ITS_Errors has `schedule_transient` or `schedule_box_root_unresolved` rows for it.

`claimed` means servicing started and did not finish. **This is self-healing by design** —
the row stays serviceable and the next cycle retries it, and every step before the final
commit is safe to repeat. Nothing is lost.

- `schedule_transient` — Box or the Worker had a blip. Wait two cycles.
- `schedule_box_root_unresolved` — the Box mirror-tree root is not configured
  (`safety_reports.box.portal_root_folder_id` — schedules file under the SAFETY root; the
  per-job folder keys off the job's PROJECT NAME joined into the pending payload, falling
  back to the raw job_id). The row is deliberately left unflagged so
  it files itself the moment that is set. **Escalate** if you do not know the value.

## Symptom 3 — "The screener flagged an upload" (MALICIOUS refuses; active content imports with a warning)

This lane inherits the manifest importer's 2026-08-11 disposition. "Active content" —
almost always a PDF carrying an auto-open instruction, an artifact most exported PDFs
have — does **not** refuse: the document imports normally with a visible warning
(ITS_Errors WARN `schedule_active_content`, and a parse note on the validate screen).
ITS itself only ever opens the bytes inside the killable sandbox. **MALICIOUS still
always refuses.**

- **MALICIOUS → escalate.** Evidence: ITS_Errors `schedule_malicious` (CRITICAL) + a
  security-flagged ITS_Review_Queue row. Nothing reached Box and no grid was created.
  The alert names the uploading account. Do not clear its flag and do not ask for a
  re-upload until Seth has reviewed the account.
- **Active content** → nothing to repair. The import proceeded; the warning is
  informational. If the office is nervous about the original in Box, a clean re-export
  (Print → Save as PDF) uploads fine — but is not required.

## Symptom 4 — "An integrity failure alert fired" — ESCALATE

**Evidence:** ITS_Errors `schedule_integrity_failed` (CRITICAL) + a security-flagged
ITS_Review_Queue row.

The bytes or the row disagree with what the Worker signed. Deliberately, the daemon posts
**no result** for these: the bytes stay in D1 so the failure can be investigated, and the
schedule stays visible in the pool.

**Escalate to Seth. Do not clear the flag, do not retry, do not delete the schedule.**

## Symptom 5 — "A schedule was refused as unreadable"

**Evidence:** an ITS_Review_Queue row saying the document could not be imported;
ITS_Errors `schedule_unreadable` (WARN). No security flag. The portal shows the schedule
`refused` with detail `ocr_failed` (the page reader crashed or timed out) or
`no_rows_recognised` (the pages read fine but no table rows were found — a cover page, a
blank export).

This is **ordinary, not a fault**. Common causes: a corrupt or truncated PDF, an export
of the wrong sheet, or a page layout the reader cannot untangle.

**Tier-2 repair:** ask the office for a fresh Smartsheet PDF export of the schedule and
have them upload that as a new revision. If you believe the original was fine and want
the daemon to try again, remove that schedule's id from
`~/its/state/schedule_poll_flagged.json` — the flag exists only to stop the same alert
firing every two minutes. **Clear a flag only for a readability refusal, never for a
security verdict or an integrity failure.**

## Symptom 6 — "schedule_creds_missing (CRITICAL)" — ESCALATE

The daemon is **fail-closed**: it will not poll at all rather than run half-configured.
One of the Worker base URL, the bearer token, or the signing secret is unavailable.

A *related but different* alert, `schedule_creds_transient` (WARN), means the base URL was
briefly unreadable — a Smartsheet blip. That one clears itself; no action.

**Escalate.** Credentials are a FIXED high-capability class.

## Symptom 7 — "schedule_bearer_rejected (CRITICAL)" — ESCALATE

The daemon's token was refused (401). The cycle stops immediately rather than burning the
whole queue against a dead token, and uploads stay queued safely.

**Escalate.** Token rotation is a secrets operation.

## Symptom 8 — "schedule_pending_fetch_sustained (CRITICAL)"

The daemon could not reach the Worker for several consecutive cycles. Uploads are queueing
unserviced but nothing is lost.

**Tier-2:** check that the portal is reachable in a browser. If it is up and this persists
past a few more cycles, **escalate**.

## Symptom 9 — "schedule_worker_rejected (ERROR + a Review-Queue row)"

The Worker PERMANENTLY refused something the daemon posted for this schedule (an HTTP
4xx — e.g. a malformed grid). The daemon one-shot-flags the schedule (`worker_rejected` in
`state/schedule_poll_flagged.json`) instead of retrying an identical rejection every cycle
forever. Rare by construction: the daemon clamps its grid to the Worker's own bounds before
posting, with a parse note per clamp that the validate screen displays.

**Tier-2:** read the Review-Queue row (it names the HTTP status and detail). If the cause
was transient tooling and the document should retry, delete that schedule's id from the
flag file — the same remediation as Symptom 5, and NEVER for an integrity/malicious flag.
A repeat on the same document escalates.

## The flag file (one-shot refusal memory)

`~/its/state/schedule_poll_flagged.json` maps a schedule's pool id to why it was fenced
(`refused`, `integrity`, `worker_rejected`). Its only job is to stop the same alert
re-firing every two minutes. Deleting an entry makes the daemon try that schedule again
on the next cycle. **Only ever clear `refused` (readability) or `worker_rejected`
entries; an `integrity` entry — and anything the screener called malicious — is Seth's.**

## What "healthy" looks like

- A fresh `schedule_poll` heartbeat in ITS_Daemon_Health every ~120 s, status OK.
- Uploaded schedules moving `pending` → `claimed` → `parsed` within a cycle or two, each
  with a row count and page previews on the validate screen.
- The original PDF visible in Box under `<job>/Schedules/`.
- ITS_Errors carrying only the per-cycle `schedule_cycle_summary` INFO line.

## Go-live (Seth only)

1. Apply migration `0066` to the live D1 **before** the Worker deploys.
2. `wrangler secret put PORTAL_SCHEDULE_API_TOKEN`, and store the same value in the
   Keychain as `ITS_PORTAL_SCHEDULE_TOKEN`.
3. Run `scripts/migrations/seed_schedule_config.py` (or confirm the two
   `field_ops.schedule_poll.*` rows exist — VC-03 checks them).
4. Confirm a clean run of the operator OCR-qualification suite over the desktop corpus
   (`tests/test_schedule_ocr_corpus.py`, operator-run — the corpus never leaves the Mac).
5. Flip `field_ops.schedule_poll.polling_enabled` to `true` and load the launchd job.
